implementation.name: GNU Bash
implementation.version_scope: GNU Bash shell scripting; shell features and external utility availability are separate concerns.

sources.label: GNU Bash features and implementation license

fit.text: Interactive command use and shell automation around existing utilities; external programs have their own dependencies.

prerequisites.text: Learn quoting, expansion, exit status and redirection before building scripts around user-supplied values.

execution.text: Bash reads shell commands; builtins and external commands participate in pipelines and redirections.

behavior.text: Bash extends sh with arrays and other features; Bash-specific scripts require Bash rather than an arbitrary sh.

tooling.text: The shell supplies history, job control and editing; a terminal and a text editor are enough for a small script.

maintenance.text: Keep the intended shell explicit and test quoting and command failures on the target environment.

costs.text: GNU Bash is free software; copying its implementation has GPL obligations distinct from utility licenses.

example.run_instructions: Save the file as hello.sh and run bash hello.sh from a terminal with GNU Bash installed.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.scope: GNU Bash implementation, not an automatic license declaration for your script.
licenses.notice: Inspect licenses of external programs separately.

implementation.name: Microsoft Bicep CLI
implementation.version_scope: Bicep-to-ARM template build workflow; the example performs no Azure deployment.

fit.text: Describe Azure resources declaratively; Bicep is infrastructure configuration rather than application request handling.

prerequisites.text: Learn Azure resource types and parameters; install the Bicep CLI to build the example locally.

execution.text: bicep build translates source into an ARM JSON template; deployment is an independent action.

behavior.text: Typed outputs expose values from a template; parameter expressions are evaluated by the deployment system.

tooling.text: The documented editor tooling supplies completion and validation for resource declarations.

maintenance.text: Resource API versions and module definitions form part of the deployment contract and should be kept with the source.

costs.text: The compiler has MIT terms; actual deployed Azure services are priced separately, so a template is not a cost estimate.

example.code:
param prefix string = 'plldn'
output resourceGroupName string = '${prefix}-dev'
example.run_instructions: Run bicep build names.bicep with the installed CLI. Inspect the generated JSON; do not deploy to exercise compilation.
example.expected_result: An ARM template contains a string parameter and an output expression. A deployment with the default parameter would produce plldn-dev.

implementation.name: GNU Bison C parser generator
implementation.version_scope: Traditional C grammar interface with user-supplied scanner, error handler and main.

sources.label: GNU Bison generated C parser interface
Bison C skeleton licence and generator source

fit.text: Generate parsers for a specified grammar; a scanner and application code complete the program.

prerequisites.text: Learn grammar productions and the generated C interface, then install Bison and a C compiler.

execution.text: Generate the parser source from a .y file, compile it, and call yyparse from main.

behavior.text: yylex returns tokens; semantic actions run when grammar productions are recognized.

tooling.text: The generator emits parsing code, but the application supplies yyerror and input handling.

maintenance.text: Preserve the parser/scanner interface when changing token definitions; avoid reserving unrelated identifiers with yy or YY prefixes.

costs.text: The generator source has GPL-3.0-or-later terms; generated-parser licensing requires checking the selected skeleton's output notices.

example.run_instructions: Run bison -o accept.c accept.y, compile accept.c with a C compiler, then run the resulting program and supply a followed by Enter.
example.expected_result: The valid input a prints accepted; another token is a syntax error.

licenses.scope: Named implementation only; dependencies and generated applications require separate review.
licenses.notice: The source licence header establishes the generator scope. Do not automatically apply that expression to every generated parser.

implementation.name: BSC Bluespec SystemVerilog compiler and Bluesim
implementation.version_scope: BSV source syntax with local simulation; BH syntax and physical synthesis flows are separate.

sources.label: BSC hardware language and tools overview
BSC simulation and compilation user guide

fit.text: Describe digital hardware with modules and rules; a simulated design is not a fabricated or timing-verified circuit.

prerequisites.text: Learn hardware state, clocks and interfaces before relying on guarded atomic actions.

execution.text: BSC produces Bluesim simulation models or Verilog for a separately selected synthesis toolchain.

behavior.text: Guarded atomic actions describe rule effects and allow the compiler to choose a scheduler.

tooling.text: BSC includes the compiler, Bluesim, standard libraries and Bluetcl; waveform tools are available separately.

maintenance.text: Review guards, clocks and scheduled rules when a hardware design changes; simulation and synthesis are distinct flows.

costs.text: Most BSC-owned source has BSD-3-Clause terms; the COPYING file lists solvers and other components with different licences.

example.run_instructions: With BSC and its simulation dependencies installed, run bsc -u -sim -g mkHello Hello.bsv, then bsc -sim -e mkHello -o hello. Run the resulting simulation executable.
example.expected_result: The simulation displays PLLDN and terminates; no hardware is deployed.

licenses.component: BSC Bluespec SystemVerilog compiler and Bluesim
licenses.scope: BSC-owned source files except component-specific exceptions listed in COPYING.
licenses.notice: Bundled solver, Haskell and other library notices remain separate.

Boogie IVL reference with currency warning

fit.text: Build verification backends or check intermediate models; accepted assertions concern the modeled program.

prerequisites.text: Learn specifications and assertions; install .NET and a supported SMT solver such as the documented default Z3.

execution.text: The tool generates verification conditions and passes them to a selected SMT solver.

behavior.text: Mathematical integer assertions describe properties; assumptions and procedure contracts determine the verification obligation.

tooling.text: Install the packaged .NET tool; solver executable paths and options can be configured explicitly.

maintenance.text: The linked language reference warns that it is dated; match advanced features to the installed tool version.

costs.text: Boogie has MIT terms; SMT solver and .NET licensing must be considered separately.

example.run_instructions: Install Boogie according to its README and provide the selected solver on PATH. Run boogie check.bpl.
example.expected_result: The arithmetic assertion is verified without a counterexample; exact report formatting depends on the tool version.

implementation.name: GNU C compiler (GCC)
implementation.version_scope: A hosted C console example using GCC and the target C library; other compilers and embedded environments differ.

sources.label: GCC compilation stages and C/C++ invocation
GNU C language introduction and reference

fit.text: Native code and interfacing with machine-level data; this hosted example requires a target C library.

prerequisites.text: Learn types, arrays and pointers alongside compilation; memory use requires explicit care.

execution.text: GCC preprocesses, compiles, assembles and links; source and object files are different stages.

behavior.text: Pointers and array access expose memory directly; language constructs do not provide automatic bounds safety.

tooling.text: Use gcc and a terminal; compiler flags select stages and target behavior.

maintenance.text: Keep target compiler and linked libraries explicit when porting between environments.

costs.text: Compiler licensing is separate from the target C library and application dependencies.

example.run_instructions: Run gcc -Wall -Wextra hello.c -o hello, then ./hello on Unix-like systems or .\hello.exe on Windows with an appropriate GCC toolchain.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.
